content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your app is mobile-first, in which case Bugsnag is the stronger choice. Rollbar is the right pick only if you want the simplest tool and won't use anything beyond error tracking.

I'm working from my knowledge, not live research. Plans and prices change often, so check the current pricing pages before you commit.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core strength** | Broadest platform: errors, performance tracing, session replay, profiling, cron monitoring, uptime | Fast, clean error grouping and real-time alerting; simple to set up | Release health and stability scores; strong mobile (iOS/Android) support |
| **SDK coverage** | Widest: most web, backend, mobile, and game frameworks | Good across mainstream languages | Good, with the deepest mobile SDKs |
| **Source maps and releases** | Mature: release tracking, suspect commits, source map upload | Solid | Solid, with good release-stability views |
| **Integrations** | Very broad (GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, PagerDuty, and more) | Adequate for common tools | Adequate for common tools |
| **Extras beyond errors** | Yes (replay, tracing, profiling) | Limited | Limited |
| **Pricing model** | Per event, with a free tier; team members are generally not the cost driver. Costs can climb with performance and replay volume. | Per event, with a free tier | Per event and/or seats, with a free tier |
| **Self-hosting** | Yes (open source) | No | No |
| **Main downside** | Can feel like a lot of tool for a small team; costs need watching if you enable every feature | Narrower scope; you'd add other tools later | Less useful outside mobile and release-health workflows |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team:**
- It covers errors now and gives you a path to performance tracing and replay later without adding a second vendor.
- The integrations with your issue tracker and chat tool are the piece your team will use every day.
- It has the largest community, so most framework questions already have answers.
- Self-hosting is available if data residency ever becomes a concern.

**When to choose differently:**
- **Bugsnag:** most of your users are on native mobile apps and you care most about crash-free session rates per release.
- **Rollbar:** you want the lowest-friction option, you don't need performance or replay, and you're comfortable adding other tools later.

**Before you decide:**
1. Check your expected monthly event volume against each free tier and the paid tier just above it. Error volume is the main cost driver.
2. Run a two-week trial of Sentry and one alternative on your staging environment. Compare how well each groups errors and how noisy the alerts are.
3. Confirm the integrations your team needs (issue tracker, chat, on-call) are on the paid plan you'd actually buy.

If you tell me your stack (languages, web vs. mobile) and rough event volume, I can narrow this down further. I can also look up current pricing if you want exact numbers.
